clue.text: Noble discovered Marie Stopes half wasted away

indicators.note: discovered here means uncovered, so Marie loses its outer letters
half of Stopes has wasted away, leaving only its first half

explanation.surface: A noble finds that the birth-control pioneer Marie Stopes has partly withered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' strips the covering letters from MARIE to leave ARI; 'half wasted away' keeps the first half of STOPES, STO.
explanation.definitionFit: An aristo is an informal shortening of aristocrat, a person of noble birth.

clue.text: Arrive at open stretch of water

definitions.meaning: to ... a place is to arrive at it
a straight, open stretch of a river between bends

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives at a stretch of open water.
explanation.definitionFit: Reach serves both as the verb of getting somewhere and as a noun for a length of river.

clue.text: Over in Paris, it is uni study which causes a headache

indicators.note: over signals the letters are turned back to front in this down clue
in means the answer sits inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A student in Paris finds that university study brings on a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to SITISUNIS lurking in 'Paris, it is uni study'; 'Over' turns it round. 'Over in Paris' looks like a French phrase to translate, but it is two separate signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the sinuses is a classic cause of a throbbing pain across the forehead.

clue.text: Dished out criticism following first two appearances of Orlando Bloom

indicators.note: following puts the criticism piece after the Orlando piece
the first two letters to appear in Orlando are taken

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold

explanation.surface: Criticism was dished out after the actor Orlando Bloom's first couple of screen appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orlando Bloom' reads as the actor's name, but Bloom is the definition, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchid is a flower, and bloom is a common crossword word for any flower.

clue.text: Grass tennis body last to install TV screens

indicators.note: screens means conceals, so the TV word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: tele is a short word for television

indicators.note: last to install means the final letter of install

parts.note: the LTA is the Lawn Tennis Association, governing British tennis

explanation.surface: An informer tips off that the tennis authority is finally fitting television screens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like the tennis surface, but it is British slang for an informer; 'screens' is the verb, to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass is British slang for an informer, and a telltale is someone who tells on others.

clue.text: 3D musical theatre production?

parts.note: 3d was three old pence (d for penny), so a 3d stage work with music suggests the Brecht-Weill piece

explanation.surface: A musical staged in three dimensions.
explanation.walkthrough: 3D looks like three-dimensional, but in pre-decimal British money d stood for penny, so 3d was threepence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Threepenny Opera is the 1928 Brecht and Weill music-theatre work.

clue.text: Tough ex-England skipper leaking 100 runs in the field

indicators.note: in places the cricketer piece within the field word

parts.note: ley, or lea, is a field or meadow

indicators.note: leaking means losing part of its contents, so letters drop out

parts.note: Mike Atherton captained England's cricket team in the 1990s
a ton is a century, 100 runs in cricket

explanation.surface: A former England cricket captain gives away a hundred runs while fielding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaking' takes TON out of ATHERTON, leaving ATHER, which goes 'in' LEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery describes meat or skin that is tough like leather.

clue.text: Pound starts to tank, heralding run on banks

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Sterling tumbles, triggering a run on the banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like the currency, but it is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound and to throb both describe a heavy repeated beating, as of a heart.

clue.text: Light, very strong amber ales freshly brewed

indicators.note: brewed afresh means the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Some light but very strong amber ales have just been brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' and 'very strong' read as describing beer, but together they define the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser produces an intense, concentrated ray of light.

clue.text: John approved this funny cat anagram

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called John approved of this amusing anagram of cat.
explanation.walkthrough: John is King John of England, who sealed the charter at Runnymede in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: King John agreed to Magna Carta under pressure from his barons.

clue.text: Hip-hop features singular harsh noise

indicators.note: features means contains, so the music word holds the letter

parts.note: rap is a style of hip-hop music
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A hip-hop track includes one particularly harsh sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a grating, scraping sound like a coarse file.

clue.text: Beat the speed of light? Speed is boring!

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so is goes inside the speed word

parts.note: haste is speed or hurry

explanation.surface: Can anything outrun light? Mere speed is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull, but it means drilling: IS goes into HASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish, and in older use specifically to beat or thrash.

clue.text: Watering hole in sweltering island capital

indicators.note: in puts the drinking place inside the heat word

parts.note: sweltering means very hot
a watering hole is informal for a bar or pub

explanation.surface: A pub on a sweltering island capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital city of Tasmania, Australia's island state.

clue.text: Join part of brass section in retirement

indicators.note: in retirement means drawing back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tuba is one instrument of an orchestra's brass section

explanation.surface: A retired musician joins a brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things abut when they are joined edge to edge or adjoin.

clue.text: US flier sailed regularly aboard Darwin's ship

indicators.note: aboard means on the ship, so letters go inside the ship's name

parts.note: HMS Beagle carried Charles Darwin on his voyage

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of sailed

explanation.surface: An American aviator sailed now and then on Darwin's famous ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ALD from 'sailed', and 'aboard' puts it in BEAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is the national bird of the United States.

clue.text: U may be so wealthy!

definitions.meaning: U is the symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: You might be that well off!
explanation.walkthrough: U reads as text-speak for you, but it is the chemical symbol for uranium.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium processed to boost its fissile isotope is called enriched, and being made rich means being well off.

clue.text: Two cricket fielders one's put under the microscope?

definitions.meaning: cover and slip are two fielding positions in cricket, slip standing beside the wicketkeeper
a thin glass square laid over a specimen on a slide

explanation.surface: A pair of cricket fielders, one of whom is subjected to close scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover slip is the thin glass square laid over a specimen on a microscope slide.

clue.text: No 1 exercise: his maths

indicators.note: to exercise is to work or put through movements, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The top exercise: his maths homework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise' looks like a noun naming the maths task, but it is a verb signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash hit is a hugely successful record, the kind that reaches number one in the charts.

clue.text: Vulgar boy having grown up as bully?

parts.note: flash means showy in a vulgar, ostentatious way
a boy who has grown up is a man

explanation.surface: A crude lad grows up to become a bully.
explanation.walkthrough: Flashman is the bully in Thomas Hughes's novel Tom Brown's School Days, set at Rugby School.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashman is literature's archetypal public-school bully, tormenting the young Tom Brown.

clue.text: Seductive woman The Count pacified?

indicators.note: someone pacified has had their anger taken away, so the anger word is removed

parts.note: Count Dracula is the most famous vampire
ire means anger

explanation.surface: A femme fatale has calmed down Count Dracula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pacified' removes IRE (anger) from VAMPIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A vamp is a woman who uses her sexual allure to exploit men, a femme fatale.

clue.text: Provide way to support dyke-builder from the south

indicators.note: to support means sitting underneath, so the road piece comes below
from the south means read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: Offa, king of Mercia, built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A road is built to back up the man who built a great earthwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the south' turns OFFA upwards to AFFO; 'to support' puts RD below it.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford can mean to provide or supply, as in trees that afford shade.

clue.text: Team's various red cards

definitions.meaning: Heart of Midlothian, an Edinburgh football club
the cards of one of the two red suits in a pack

explanation.surface: A football team receives a number of red cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Red cards suggest sendings-off, but here they are playing cards of a red suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts names both a Scottish football club and a red suit in a deck of playing cards.

clue.text: Severe, without passion, not feminine

indicators.note: not means leaving out, so the letter for feminine is removed

parts.note: frigid means cold and lacking passion

explanation.surface: Someone stern, cold and unwomanly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not feminine' takes F from FRIGID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid can describe strict, inflexible and severe rules or people.

clue.text: Concerning former president: 'I have a stroke'

parts.note: of can mean about or concerning
FDR is Franklin Delano Roosevelt, US president
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: An ex-president announces that he has suffered a stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: The stroke reads as a medical event, but it is a cricket shot.
explanation.definitionFit: An off drive is a cricket shot hit straight-ish on the off side of the field.

clue.text: Celebrity hero skinned snake

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person, a celebrity

indicators.note: skinned means having its outer layer removed, so hero loses its end letters

explanation.surface: A famous hero has been flayed by a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The viper is a venomous snake, the adder being Britain's species.

clue.text: Eager to review odd Georgian characters

indicators.note: to review is to look back, so the letters are read backwards
odd picks the letters in odd positions of Georgian
characters confirms it is letters of Georgian being picked

explanation.surface: Keen to look back at some odd Georgian personalities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' takes GOGA from Georgian; 'to review' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited and impatient to know or see something.

clue.text: Picture gory pile writhing around on rugby pitch?

indicators.note: around means the goalpost letters stand at either side

parts.note: rugby goalposts are H-shaped and stand at both ends of the pitch, giving two Hs

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gory heap of bodies writhing on a rugby pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' makes IEROGLYP from GORY PILE, and 'around' sets an H, the shape of each set of posts, at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A hieroglyph is a pictorial symbol used as writing, as in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Sell deathtrap, occasionally the cause of bitter feud

parts.note: vend means sell

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter of deathtrap is taken

explanation.surface: Selling a dangerous building sometimes sparks a bitter quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged blood feud between families or people.

clue.text: Send abroad record gold — 500 tons (about)

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the number and weight letters go round the others

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
an EP is an extended-play record
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Ship overseas a gold disc and five hundred tons of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed 'about' looks like an approximation of the tonnage, but it means the letters for 500 and tons go round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To deport is to expel someone from a country, sending them overseas.
